questions.text: Did you know that something as simple as a paper plane inspired real scientiﬁ c explorations of ﬂ ight?
In Grade 7, we will try to ask deeper questions: How do things work?
Why do events happen the way they do?
And what can we learn from the patterns that we see in nature?
We will start by looking at the properties of materials around us, mostly the things we experience but perhaps never ask questions about — why are some fruits sour?
What happens when we wash a haldi stain on our school uniform?
Especially around the middle-school years, our bodies are changing rapidly! Why?
Don’t plants also need food to grow?
How do they get their food?
We get prepared to go to school in the morning and are ready to sleep at night but have you thought about how we measure time?
And how fast does something happen?
Isn’t it amazing that we humans can wonder about the wonderful world we live in?

There are never any wrong questions, so let your imagination run wild! Since such exercises might not be very familiar, here is an example to help you! Suppose the answer was ‘just make it half!’ — what all could this be a response to?
Well, it could range from “How do we ensure getting equal shares of cake?” to “My essay is too long”, or “I can’t ﬁ t this in the envelope” or even “I cannot dance to such a long song”...

all very diﬀ erent! So, let’s see what kind of creative questions you can ask! (Please ask a more interesting, and not obvious questions like “What is 32+10?”, or even “What is the answer to life, the universe, and everything?”) Answer: Because the cat’s teeth were crooked.
